actions.action: Inspect leaf undersides and new leaves with a flashlight or magnifier for thrips or other pests
Check soil and water only when the top 2-3 inches are dry
Use a pot with drainage holes
Move the plant to bright, indirect light with good airflow
Inspect the plant weekly, including leaf undersides and stems, for spreading spots
If spots grow, develop halos or turn mushy, remove the affected leaves
If spots spread, apply a copper fungicide or broad-spectrum treatment
If pests are found, treat with insecticidal soap or neem
Isolate the plant from other plants if more spots appear

reason: The answer lists fungal leaf spot only as an unlikely second possibility and offers fungicide only as a conditional step, while telling the owner not to cut leaves and to treat the spots as cosmetic, which likely delays the fungicide treatment that fixed it.
